# 🕉️ RAMAYANA — ADI KAVYA
## MASTER PROMPT FILE (Merged) — Version 7.1
### Bible + Script Prompt + Production Prompt + Workflow Guide, in one document — now with the Image/Audio Tag System

This single file merges the four original documents (`01_The_Bible`, `02_Script_Prompt`, `03_Production_Prompt`, `04_Workflow_Guide`) exactly as they were, with one addition: a **Tag System** for the audio/narration output and every image prompt, so outputs are numbered, self-contained, and copy-paste ready — the same tagging approach used in the Sacred Stories & Ancient Temples engine.

**Nothing else has been changed.** All rules, laws, formats, and checklists below are unchanged from v7.0 except where marked with the 🏷️ tag-system additions.

---

## 📑 TABLE OF CONTENTS

1. WORKFLOW GUIDE — how to use this file
2. THE BIBLE — static reference (Character Bible, Location Bible, Visual Style, Religious Accuracy Law, Negative Prompt, Style Tags)
3. SCRIPT PROMPT — creative pass (run first)
4. PRODUCTION PROMPT — asset pass (run second)

---
---

# PART 1 — 🕉️ WORKFLOW GUIDE
## How to Use the Split System
### Version 7.0

---

## THE THREE DOCUMENTS (now three PARTS of this one file)

1. **THE BIBLE** — Static reference. Save it once. Paste it alongside the other prompts when needed. Contains: Character Bible, Location Bible, Visual Style, Religious Accuracy Law, Universal Negative Prompt, Universal Style Tags.

2. **THE SCRIPT PROMPT** — Creative pass. Run FIRST. Its only job: take raw content → output locked Hindi script (Sections 1, 2, 2B). Nothing about images, motion, or overlays.

3. **THE PRODUCTION PROMPT** — Asset pass. Run SECOND. Its only job: take locked script + Bible → output all visual assets (Sections 3, 3B, 4, 5). Does NOT modify the script.

---

## WORKFLOW PER VIDEO

### STEP 1: PREPARE INPUTS

**For the Script Prompt, provide:**
```
Type: A (Story) or B (Fact)
Title: [Optional — if not provided, AI generates from content]
Content: [The story or fact content]
```

**Example:**
```
Type: A
Title: "विश्वामित्र का सिद्ध आश्रम से मिथिला की यात्रा"
Content: [Sarga 31-32 content, or any story summary]
```

### STEP 2: RUN SCRIPT PROMPT

Paste the Script Prompt + your content input.

**What you get back:**
- Section 1: Full script with scenes, timing, emotion beats, on-screen text
- Section 2: ElevenLabs TTS script with timestamps
- Section 2B: Paste-ready voiced script for ElevenLabs, wrapped in `<script>...</script>` 🏷️

**Review the script.** Read it aloud. Check:
- [ ] Hook has emotion + mystery (one withheld fact)
- [ ] Re-hook exists at ~50–60% mark
- [ ] CTA is ONE line, max 3 seconds
- [ ] All in simple Devanagari Hindi, no emotion tags
- [ ] Story feels complete before CTA

**If needed, ask for revisions.** Only move to Step 3 when the script is locked.

### STEP 3: RUN PRODUCTION PROMPT

Paste:
1. The Production Prompt
2. The locked script (copy-paste Sections 1, 2, 2B from Step 2, including the `<script>` tag)
3. The Bible (or reference it: "Use Character Bible and Location Bible from the Bible document")

**What you get back:**
- Section 3: Leonardo.AI image prompts (Thumbnail + Scene images + Follow Frame + End Card), each wrapped in its own numbered `<image_prompt>...</image_prompt>` 🏷️
- Section 3B: Gemini motion prompts for exactly 3 images, each cross-referencing its `<image_prompt>` tag number 🏷️
- Section 4: All Hindi text overlays for video editor
- Section 5: Reflection Engine prompt for comments

### STEP 4: PRODUCE

1. **Generate images** in Leonardo.AI using Section 3 prompts (copy the contents of each `<image_prompt>` block)
2. **Generate motion** in Google Gemini using Section 3B prompts (3 images only)
3. **Record narration** in ElevenLabs using the Section 2B script (copy the contents of the `<script>` block)
4. **Assemble** in video editor: narration + motion clips + static images + text overlays per Section 4
5. **Post** with reflection prompt from Section 5

---

## WHY THIS FIXES THE PROBLEMS

| Problem | How the split fixes it |
|---|---|
| AI forgets instructions | Each prompt has ~15 rules instead of ~50. Fewer competing constraints = higher compliance. |
| Random sections skipped | Each prompt has ONE job. Script Prompt never touches images. Production Prompt never touches script. No silent drops. |
| Hook lacks curiosity | Script Prompt has a dedicated Hook Rules section with the Emotion + Mystery formula. Enforceable because it's not competing with 40 other rules. |
| CTA too long | Script Prompt enforces ONE line, max 3 seconds. No exceptions. |
| Missing re-hook | Script Prompt has a dedicated Midpoint Re-Hook Rule with formula and examples. Checked in final checklist. |
| Inconsistent output | Smaller rule sets per generation = the model can hold all of them in working memory. |
| Copy-paste errors across tools 🏷️ | The `<script>` and `<image_prompt>` tags make each asset a self-contained, unambiguous block — nothing to accidentally merge or crop when moving between ElevenLabs, Leonardo, and Gemini. |

---

## TOKEN EFFICIENCY

- **Old system:** One mega-prompt (~8,000 tokens) → one generation
- **New system:** Bible (~2,500 tokens, saved once) + Script Prompt (~3,000 tokens) + Production Prompt (~3,000 tokens) = ~8,500 tokens total, but split across TWO focused generations
- **Result:** Each generation has a smaller, more enforceable instruction set. The Bible is reference, not regenerated.

---
---

# PART 2 — 🕉️ THE BIBLE (Static Reference)
### Version 7.0 — Split Architecture

This document is a STATIC REFERENCE. It does not change per video. Keep it saved and paste it alongside the Script Prompt or Production Prompt whenever those prompts need character, location, or visual-style information.

---

## 👥 CHARACTER BIBLE — NEVER CHANGE THESE DESCRIPTIONS

Copy the relevant character details into EVERY image prompt. These descriptions must never change across content.

### 🔵 RAMA
- **Age:** 25–30 years old
- **Skin:** Deep blue-dark complexion (called "shyama varna" in the Ramayana) — this is non-negotiable and must never be shown as fair or light
- **Face:** Strong jaw, high forehead, calm and powerful eyes, slightly arched eyebrows
- **Body:** Tall, broad shoulders, long arms that reach almost to his knees (this is a divine sign called "ajanubahu")
- **Hair:** Long black hair — tied in a bun or loose warrior style when in the forest
- **Palace clothes:** Yellow/gold dhoti (lower garment), ornate crown (mukut), gold jewelry, his bow called Sharanga
- **Forest/Exile clothes:** Saffron or ochre bark-cloth dhoti, matted tied-up hair (jata), no crown, carries bow and quiver of arrows
- **Expression:** Always calm, dignified, and divine — never angry or worried-looking

### 🌟 SITA
- **Age:** 20–25 years old
- **Skin:** Golden-fair complexion (called "suvarna varna") with a soft natural glow
- **Face:** Large expressive eyes, gentle expression, oval face, long black hair
- **Palace clothes:** Red and gold silk saree, ornate jewelry, flowers in her hair
- **Forest clothes:** Simple ochre or cream-colored saree, minimal jewelry, hair braided
- **Lanka captivity clothes:** Worn yellow or white saree, slightly disheveled hair, sad eyes, no jewelry or ornaments
- **Expression:** Graceful, strong, and full of devotion — never shown as weak or helpless

### 🏹 LAKSHMANA
- **Age:** 22–27 years old
- **Skin:** Fair wheatish complexion
- **Face:** Sharp warrior features, alert and watchful eyes, strong jaw
- **Body:** Very muscular, slightly shorter than Rama
- **Palace clothes:** Green or blue dhoti, warrior armor, ornaments
- **Forest/Exile clothes:** Bark-cloth style same as Rama — always carrying his bow
- **Expression:** Alert, fiercely loyal, always protective of Rama and Sita

### 🐒 HANUMAN
- **Form:** Large, powerful Vanara (divine monkey) body — orange-brown fur, monkey face with deeply devoted eyes
- Stands upright like a human, very muscular, tail curled behind him
- **Clothes:** Simple loincloth (kaupin), sacred thread across his chest (janeu)
- May carry a mace (gada) depending on the scene
- **Expression:** Full of devotion, mighty, and fearless
- **Size:** State clearly in each prompt — normal human size OR mountain-large (vishwaroopa/giant form)

### 👑 RAVANA
- **Age:** 40–50 years old — powerful and commanding dark presence
- **Skin:** Dark complexion with a red or dark undertone
- **Face:** Ten heads — show ALL ten heads in wide grand shots; show only his main dominant head in close-up shots (say clearly which style you want in each prompt)
- **Body:** Massive, very imposing, royal bearing
- **Clothes:** Dark red and black royal robes, gold crown on each head, multiple arms holding weapons
- **Expression:** Arrogant power, controlled rage — commanding, never mocking or cartoonish

### 👴 DASHARATHA
- **Age:** ~60 years old — elderly, dignified king
- **Skin:** Fair, aged complexion with grey beard and grey hair
- **Clothes:** White and gold royal dhoti, elaborate crown, royal jewelry
- **Expression:** Dignified, emotionally heavy — a man carrying great grief

### 👸 KAIKEYI
- **Age:** ~45 years old
- **Skin:** Fair, regal bearing
- **Clothes:** Rich silk queen's attire, prominent jewelry
- **Expression:** Calculated ambition OR deep grief depending on the scene — specify in each prompt

### 🤴 BHARATA
- **Age:** 22–25 years old
- **Skin:** Fair, resembles his father Dasharatha
- **Body:** Similar build to Lakshmana, noble appearance
- **Clothes:** Royal or simple depending on the scene
- **Expression:** Deep grief-stricken devotion for Rama

### 🌿 VIBHISHANA
- **Age:** 35–40 years old
- **Skin:** Dark like Ravana but with softer, kinder features
- **Clothes:** Rakshasa (demon) royal clothing but simpler and less decorated than Ravana's
- **Expression:** Righteous, calm, walking the path of dharma (righteousness)

---

## 🗺️ LOCATION BIBLE — FIXED VISUAL RULES

### 🏛️ AYODHYA PALACE
- Grand ancient Indian architecture — tall stone pillars, carved arched gateways, richly decorated stone walls
- Warm gold and amber lighting, silk drapes, oil lamps, flower garlands, ceremonial fire
- Surroundings: lush royal gardens, chariots, elephants, peacocks
- Era: Pure Treta Yuga (an ancient divine age) — absolutely zero modern elements

### 🌿 DANDAKA / PANCHAVATI FOREST
- Dense ancient Indian jungle — very tall trees, thick canopy above, hanging roots, drifting mist
- Lighting: filtered green-gold sunlight in daytime, or dark firelit atmosphere at night
- The forest hermitage (ashram): simple thatched huts, deer resting nearby, a sacred fire burning (dhuni)

### 🏔️ CHITRAKUTA
- Peaceful forested hills, flowing streams, birds all around
- Simple and beautiful — a strong visual contrast to the grandeur of Ayodhya

### 🏰 LANKA
- Magnificent golden city sitting on top of a mountain, surrounded by a vast ocean on all sides
- Architecture: grand but ominous — gold and black stone, towering spires, richly decorated but with a dark feel
- Atmosphere: dramatic storm clouds OR blazing sunset always work well here

### 🌸 ASHOKA VATIKA (GARDEN IN LANKA)
- A lush garden with flowering trees — especially ashoka trees (these are the key detail)
- Well-kept but feels like a prison — beautiful yet melancholic
- Sita is always shown seated under an ashoka tree in this location

### 🦍 KISHKINDHA
- Rocky hills, cave entrances, dense forest all around
- The Vanara (monkey) kingdom — natural cave palaces carved into the mountainside

### 🌊 OCEAN SHORE / RAM SETU BRIDGE
- Vast ancient ocean, dramatic sky — sunrise or sunset lighting
- Rocky coastline, the entire Vanara army stretching to the horizon
- Ram Setu bridge: large floating boulders with Nala (the divine architect) directing the construction

---

## 🎨 LOCKED VISUAL STYLE (Apply to ALL Images)

- **Camera style:** Cinematic photography, ultra-realistic
- **Lighting style:** Volumetric light, dramatic rim lighting, golden hour or divine glow
- **Color tone / grade:** Warm gold and amber for palace/devotion scenes; cool green-gold for forest; dark gold-black for Lanka; soft pastels for Chitrakuta
- **Overall mood:** Sacred grandeur, devotional epic atmosphere, photorealistic textures, 8K resolution, emotionally powerful composition
- **Era:** Pure Treta Yuga ancient India — zero modern elements

---

## ⚠️ RELIGIOUS ACCURACY LAW — NON-NEGOTIABLE

- **Rama** MUST always be shown with his blue-dark complexion, bow, and noble bearing — never fair or light skin
- **Sita** MUST always be shown with her golden radiance, framed with respect and dignity
- **Hanuman** MUST always be shown with deep devotion — powerful but never frightening or monstrous
- **Ravana** is the villain — show him as powerful and commanding, never mocking or cartoonish
- Sacred fire (agni), forehead marks (tilak), sacred thread (janeu), and other holy symbols must always be depicted correctly
- **Treta Yuga only** — absolutely zero modern elements, no modern clothes, no modern buildings, no modern objects
- Always show ancient Indian geography and architecture

---

## 🖼️ UNIVERSAL NEGATIVE PROMPT (Use for ALL Leonardo Images)

cartoon, anime, illustration, modern clothing, modern architecture, western facial features, plastic-looking skin, wrong skin color for Rama (must be blue-dark, never fair), disrespectful depiction of any deity or sacred figure, blurry image, watermark, text in image (except for thumbnail and follow frame)

---

## 🖼️ UNIVERSAL STYLE TAGS (Use for ALL Leonardo Images)

ultra realistic, cinematic photography, Treta Yuga ancient India, devotional epic atmosphere, volumetric light, [this content's lighting style], [this content's color grade], photorealistic textures, 8K resolution, emotionally powerful composition, sacred grandeur

---
---

# PART 3 — 🕉️ SCRIPT PROMPT (Creative Pass — Run FIRST)
### Version 7.0 — Split Architecture

Your ONLY job is to take raw content and output a locked, approved Hindi script. You do NOT generate images, thumbnails, motion prompts, overlays, or reflection prompts. Those come later in the Production Prompt.

---

## ⚙️ STEP 0 — CONTENT ANALYSIS (SILENT)

Before writing, identify silently:

1. **CONTENT TYPE** — Type A (Story) or Type B (Fact)
2. **TITLE** — If I provide a title, use it. If I don't, create the most emotionally compelling Hindi title from the content.
3. **EMOTIONAL HOOK** — The single most powerful opening line (3–6 words) that carries the core emotion AND plants a mystery. See Hook Rules below.
4. **MIDPOINT RE-HOOK** — One line (5–8 words) that re-ignites curiosity at roughly the 50–60% mark of the script.
5. **KEY CHARACTERS** — who appears
6. **LOCATION(S)** — match the Location Bible exactly
7. **TIME OF DAY & MOOD** — morning, night, storm, peaceful, etc.
8. THE CORE EMOTION — the single feeling this must leave in the viewer's heart. Choose ONE:
   - Devotion (भक्ति)
   - Grief (शोक)
   - Awe (विस्मय)
   - Inspiration (प्रेरणा)
   - Righteous anger (धार्मिक क्रोध)
   - Tender love (स्नेह)
   - Solitude (विरह)

❤️ EMOTION EXTRACTION LAW (NEW — NON-NEGOTIABLE)

When the source material appears informational, descriptive, historical, or emotionally neutral, you MUST identify the strongest hidden human emotion within the event and build the narration around that emotion.

Facts do not create retention.
Human emotions create retention.

Before writing any narration, ask:
"What would the people in this moment have felt?"

Then make that feeling the emotional spine of the script.

EMOTION EXTRACTION PRIORITY:
1. Devotion (भक्ति)
2. Sacrifice (त्याग)
3. Loss (वियोग)
4. Love (प्रेम)
5. Hope (आशा)
6. Fear (भय)
7. Wonder (विस्मय)
8. Duty (कर्तव्य)
9. Courage (साहस)

CRITICAL RULE:
Never narrate events.
Narrate what the events MEAN to the people experiencing them.

Viewers remember feelings.
They forget information.

9. **SCRIPT LENGTH & IMAGE COUNT PLAN** — based on content complexity:
   - 45–75 second script → 5 to 8 scene images
   - 75–105 second script → 8 to 12 scene images
   - Complex scenes (battle, vision, divine moment) → use 2 images for that scene
   - Always add: 1 Thumbnail + 1 Follow Frame + 1 End Card
   - Total images = scene images + 3

---

## 🎯 HOOK RULES — EMOTION + MYSTERY (NON-NEGOTIABLE)

The first 3 seconds must make the viewer FEEL something sacred AND want to know what happens next.

### THE FORMULA:
**Emotion + One Withheld Fact = Unstoppable Hook**

The hook must name a feeling the viewer already knows, AND leave one critical piece of information unsaid.

| Weak (emotion only) | Strong (emotion + mystery) |
|---|---|
| "उस रात... कोई नहीं सोया।" | "उस रात... अयोध्या में कोई नहीं सोया।" |
| "उसने कहा — राम। बस।" | "एक शब्द ने पूरी सेना बचा ली।" |
| "धनुष उठा... और हवा रुक गई।" | "यह धनुष पहले कोई नहीं उठा सका था।" |
| "पीछे मुड़कर देखा... कोई नहीं था।" | "पीछे मुड़कर देखा... अयोध्या जल रही थी।" |

### RULES:
- Hook is 3–6 words in Hindi
- It must carry the core emotion
- It must withhold ONE specific fact that the viewer needs the story to answer
- Never explain in the hook — evoke and withhold
- The Emotional Hook MUST be the very first spoken line. Nothing before it.

### ❌ NEVER START WITH:
- "Aaj hum baat karenge..."
- "Yeh kahani hai..."
- "Is episode mein..."
- "Ramayana — Adi Kavya..."
- Series title card
- Content number
- Any text that feels like a news headline or clickbait

---

## 🎯 MANDATORY NARRATION OPENING STRUCTURE

After the Emotional Hook lands, the narrator MUST go DIRECTLY into the story.

```
[EMOTIONAL HOOK] ← FIRST and ONLY thing spoken

(short pause)

[STORY NARRATION BEGINS IMMEDIATELY]
```

### RULES:
- The Emotional Hook MUST be the very first spoken line. No exceptions.
- After the hook, there is a short pause.
- Then the story narration begins IMMEDIATELY.
- NO "Ramayana — Adi Kavya" announcement.
- NO series intro. NO episode number. NOTHING before the hook.
- Content titles are NOT spoken by the narrator.

---

## 🎯 MIDPOINT RE-HOOK RULE (NEW — NON-NEGOTIABLE)

At approximately 50–60% of the script length, insert ONE line that re-ignites curiosity.

### THE FORMULA:
**A surprising fact or reversal that makes the viewer realize the story is bigger than they thought.**

### EXAMPLES:
- "सीता ने बचपन में शिव धनुष उठा लिया था।" → Story continues → "लेकिन यही बात बाद में पूरी दुनिया के लिए चुनौती बन गई।" → Story continues
- "राम ने वन में शांति पा ली थी।" → Story continues → "लेकिन रावण की नज़र अब उन पर थी।" → Story continues
- "हनुमान ने सोचा काम हो गया।" → Story continues → "लेकिन लंका की दीवारों के पीछे कुछ और इंतज़ार कर रहा था।" → Story continues

### RULES:
- Re-hook is 5–8 words max
- It must appear at roughly the 50–60% mark of the total script
- It must introduce a new tension, reversal, or withheld fact
- It must feel natural to the story flow — not forced
- After the re-hook, the story continues to its ending

---

## 📜 SECTION 1 — SCRIPT

**LANGUAGE:** Simple, easy Hindi — but with the rhythm and weight of a temple katha. Short sentences that land like bells. Repetition that feels like chanting, not like a mistake.
**STYLE:** Sacred storytelling — a wise elder speaking to your heart at the hour when the lamps are lit
**DURATION:** 45–105 seconds — match the story/fact length, never cut content just to fit a time limit
**PACING:** The story breathes. Pauses where the heart needs time. Acceleration where fate moves. Something emotionally new every 5–8 seconds.

---

### 🎭 EMOTIONAL PACING RULE

| Story Beat | Pacing | What the viewer feels |
|---|---|---|
| Sacred or divine moment | Very slow, whispered | Awe, reverence |
| Grief or loss | Slow, with pauses | Sadness, empathy |
| Action or battle | Faster, urgent | Tension, excitement |
| Realization or turning point | Pause, then revelation | Understanding, shock |
| Devotional peak | Slow, powerful, resonant | Connection to the divine |

**Rule:** Never use the same pacing for more than 15 seconds. But the shifts should feel natural, like breathing — not artificial, like a machine.

---

### 📝 SCRIPT FORMAT:

```
🎬 SCENE [N] — [SCENE TITLE]
Duration: [X seconds]
Emotion: [What the viewer should feel in this scene]

Visual: [What we see — location, characters, what is happening]
Camera: [extreme close-up / wide / low angle / overhead / etc.]

LINE [N]:
Text: [Hindi narration — simple words, emotional weight, sacred rhythm]
Tone: [devotional / dramatic / sorrowful / powerful / divine / whisper / tense / warm]
Speed: [slow / medium / fast]
Pause: [where the narrator pauses for effect]
On-Screen Text: [Text that appears WITH this line — 2-4 words max, or NONE. Must carry emotion, not information]
```

---

### 📲 SACRED ENDING — AFTER THE STORY IS COMPLETE

**ENDING ORDER (ALWAYS IN THIS ORDER):**
1. Story ending — either a powerful closing line OR a devotional closing line that leaves the viewer with the core emotion
2. **NO follow line —** the Follow Frame (with embedded CTA) handles this visually
3. **NO separate Like/Comment/Subscribe CTAs in narration** — all CTAs are embedded in the Follow Frame visually and narrated in ONE ultra-short line
4. **NO next episode tease** — each story stands alone

**Why this matters:**
- The story must feel complete before anything else is asked
- The final 20 seconds must NOT feel like a "sales pitch" — that's why viewers leave
- All CTA is compressed into ONE line + the Follow Frame visual
- The viewer should feel the story ended beautifully, and the CTA feels like a gentle blessing, not a transaction

---

## 🎙️ SECTION 2 — ELEVENLABS TTS SCRIPT (WITH TIMESTAMPS)

This section is the narration formatted with timestamps for easy editing in video software.

**Rules:**
- No scene labels, no visual descriptions — pure narration only
- Use `"..."` for natural pauses where the narrator breathes or pauses for effect
- Timestamps every 6–10 seconds
- Devotional, epic pacing throughout — not rushed, but alive
- Hook is preserved exactly from Section 1 — the first words spoken carry the core emotion + mystery
- **NO series announcement — story begins immediately after the hook**
- Content titles are NOT spoken
- **NO separate follow line, like CTA, comment CTA, subscribe CTA, or next episode tease in narration**
- Instead: ONE ultra-short closing blessing line that includes the CTA naturally
- Use only simple, easy Hindi words throughout

---

### FORMAT:

```
[0:00 – 0:04]
[EMOTIONAL HOOK — first and only spoken line before story]

[0:04 – 0:08]
[Story narration begins immediately...]

[0:08 – 0:16]
Narration...
```

*(Continue until the end)*

**END ORDER IN TIMESTAMPS:**
```
[X:XX – X:XX]
[Story ending line — powerful or devotional close that leaves the core emotion]

[X:XX – X:XX]
[ONE ultra-short closing line — natural voice, warm tone: "जय श्री राम लिखकर जुड़े रहिए। 🙏" — MAXIMUM 3 SECONDS]
```

---

## 🎙️ SECTION 2B — ELEVENLABS COMPLETE VOICED SCRIPT (PASTE-READY)

This is the ONLY section you need to paste into ElevenLabs. It contains EVERYTHING the narrator speaks — from the very first word to the very last.

**What is included (in this exact order):**
1. **Emotional Hook** — the first line opens with pure feeling + mystery. No series title, no content number.
2. **Short pause** — `(break)` after the hook
3. **Full story/fact narration** — with natural emotion and pauses — USE ONLY SIMPLE EASY HINDI WORDS IN DEVANAGARI
4. **Midpoint Re-Hook** — appears naturally within the story flow at ~50–60% mark
5. **Story ending** — powerful or devotional closing line that leaves the core emotion
6. **ONE ultra-short CTA line** — maximum 3 seconds, warm natural voice

**CRITICAL OPENING ORDER:**
```
[EMOTIONAL HOOK]

(break)

[STORY NARRATION BEGINS IMMEDIATELY]
```

**NO "Ramayana — Adi Kavya." NO series intro. NOTHING before the hook. The hook IS the opening.**

**Language Rule:** Use only simple, everyday Hindi words throughout in Devanagari script. If any word feels hard or old-fashioned, replace it with the simple Hindi word that means the same. Every viewer — young or old — should understand every single word without difficulty. But the words must carry WEIGHT.

**Rules:**
- No timestamps, no labels, no formatting at all
- Pure narration only — exactly as it should be spoken aloud
- **NO emotion tags like (whisper), (sad), (dramatic) — ElevenLabs v2 does NOT support these.**
- Instead: Use natural language cues, punctuation, and spacing to create emotion
- Use `...` for breathing pauses
- Use `—` for emotional pauses
- Use line breaks for longer pauses
- Everything voiced — nothing left for manual text overlay
- Content titles are NEVER spoken by the narrator
- **CRITICAL: The CTA is ONE line only, max 3 seconds. No separate follow/like/comment/subscribe lines.**

---

### 🏷️ AUDIO TAG SYSTEM FOR SECTION 2B (NEW)

The complete Section 2B narration must be wrapped in a single `<script>` tag so it is one self-contained, paste-ready block for ElevenLabs.

Rules:

* The entire Section 2B output — hook through CTA — goes inside exactly one `<script>...</script>` block.
* Nothing goes outside the tag: no headers, no labels, no notes, no timestamps.
* Do not split Section 2B into multiple `<script>` blocks — it is always exactly one block per video.
* The content inside the tag must be pure narration text only, formatted per the rules above (`...` pauses, `—` emotional pauses, `(break)` for longer pauses, line breaks).

Required structure:

```text
<script>
[भावनात्मक हुक — 3-6 शब्द]

(break)

[पूरी कहानी — री-हुक सहित]

(break)

[कहानी समाप्ति पंक्ति]

(break)

[एक ही पंक्ति में CTA]
</script>
```

---

### 🎭 ELEVENLABS v2 NATURAL VOICE GUIDE

**⚠️ CRITICAL: ElevenLabs v2 does NOT support (parentheses) emotion tags. They will be read aloud as text. DO NOT USE THEM.**

Instead, create emotion through:

| Effect | How to achieve it in v2 |
|---|---|
| Whisper / Soft | Use short sentences. End with `...` Add line break before. Write words that FEEL soft. |
| Sad / Heavy | Use repetition. Use words like "phir bhi," "lekin," "magar." Add `...` after emotional words. |
| Powerful / Epic | Use strong verbs. Short punchy sentences. End with `।` or `!` |
| Devotional | Use sacred words: "prabhu," "bhagwan," "kripa." Gentle rhythm. |
| Tense / Urgent | Short fragments. No pauses. Rapid delivery through tight wording. |
| Warm / Gentle | Use words like "beta," "pyaar," "sneh." Softer vowel sounds. |

**How to use:** Write naturally. Let the WORDS carry the emotion. The AI voice will follow the natural rhythm of Hindi.

### 🖼️ THUMBNAIL RULES — HIGH-CTR DESIGN

**GOAL:** A thumbnail so compelling that scrolling thumbs STOP. When converted to motion, the text and key visual elements must remain perfectly readable.

**Design Principles:**
1. **THE "FACE + FEELING" RULE:** Show an extreme close-up of a character's face expressing the core emotion — tears, devotion, anger, awe. Human faces stop thumbs better than anything else.
2. **DRAMATIC LIGHTING:** Use rim lighting, golden hour glow, or divine light rays. The face must GLOW.
3. **ASYMMETRIC COMPOSITION:** Never center the subject dead-middle. Use rule of thirds. Place the face on the left or right third, with negative space on the opposite side for text.
4. **TEXT AS DESIGN ELEMENT:** The text is NOT just overlay — it's part of the image composition.
   - Use **bold Devanagari font** with **heavy dark outer glow/stroke** (not just a simple outline)
   - Text color: **Gold gradient or pure white** — never plain
   - Text placement: **Lower third or bottom corner** — never blocking the face
   - Text size: **Large enough to read at thumbnail size (154x86px on mobile)**
   - Text content: **3–6 words MAX** — emotional, not informational
   - Add a **subtle shadow or glow behind text** so it pops against any background
5. **COLOR CONTRAST:** Use complementary colors. If the background is warm (gold/orange), text should be cool (white/blue glow). If background is cool (blue/dark), text should be warm (gold/orange glow).
6. **INTRIGUE WITHOUT CLICKBAIT:** The thumbnail should make the viewer FEEL "I need to know what happens here" — not "this looks fake."
7. **MOTION-READY:** When this image gets Gemini motion, the text must remain readable. So:
   - Text should be on a relatively static part of the image
   - Avoid placing text over areas that will have heavy motion (flowing hair, moving fabric)
   - The face can have subtle motion (breathing, blinking) — text stays sharp

**Thumbnail Text Examples:**
- "राम का वनवास..." (face of Rama, looking back with sorrow)
- "सीता हरण!" (Sita's terrified eye close-up)
- "हनुमान का चमत्कार" (Hanuman's face glowing with divine light)
- "रावण का अंत" (Ravana's ten heads silhouetted against fire)
- "एक तीर... एक लक्ष्य" (Rama's hand drawing bow, face intense)

**❌ NEVER:**
- Plain text in the middle with a generic background
- Stock-looking images
- Text at the top (gets cropped on some platforms)
- More than 6 words of text
- Cartoonish or anime style
